newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-SPANISH REFEREE CLEARED BY FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH REFEREE CLEARED BY FIFA.

text.p: FIFA, world soccer's governing body, on Wednesday cleared Spanish referee Manuel Diaz Vega of bribery allegations connected with a World Cup qualifying match between Switzerland and Norway last November.

The allegations, which were published in various Swiss newspapers, first surfaced during a UEFA investigation into Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger, who received a life ban on March 27 for attempting to fix a European Cup match between Grasshopper Zurich and Auxerre.

Blick, a Swiss-German tabloid, had claimed its sports editor, Rainer Meier, had been approached by Roethlisberger asking if the paper were interested in having Diaz Vega, the official in charge of the group three match, whistle in favour of the Swiss.

Meier, who has since been dismissed as sports editor, alleged Roethlisberger had come to him four days before the November 10 match and told him he knew the Spanish referee and that the game could be bought for 100,000 Swiss francs ($69,500). Norway won the match 1-0.
A FIFA inquiry declared that it had "absolute confidence in the integrity of Manuel Diaz Vega".
"The Disciplinary Committee concluded that there was no indication or reason to believe that bribery or attempted bribery had taken place," the inquiry said in a press release.
The inquiry met Diaz Vega, FIFA match commissioner Louis Kilcoyne and Roethlisberger at FIFA headquarters in Zurich last Thursday.

Their investigation determined that while Diaz Vega and Roethlisberger may have known each other, having participated in UEFA referee courses, and that while Roethlisberger had attended the Switzerland-Norway match as a spectator, he had absolutely no contact with Diaz Vega. ($ = 1.438 Swiss Francs)
